crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Self-Driving Laboratories
children.blurb: Self-driving laboratories are experimental platforms that combine automated hardware, sensors, and machine learning to plan, execute, and interpret experiments with limited human intervention.

children.name: Digital Twins for Experiments
children.blurb: A digital twin for an experiment is a live computational model of a physical laboratory setup, its instruments, samples, and protocols, used to plan, monitor, and interpret runs.

children.name: Instrument and Sensor Data
children.blurb: Instrument and sensor data in laboratory automation and simulation covers the raw and processed signals from analytical instruments, environmental sensors, imaging systems, and robotic lab equipment.

children.name: Optimising Lab Protocols
children.blurb: Optimising lab protocols uses AI and simulation to refine the sequence, timing, and parameters of experimental procedures.

children.name: Forecasting Lab Supplies
children.blurb: Forecasting lab supplies means predicting future demand for consumables, reagents, equipment parts, and other inventory in research and clinical laboratories.

sections.body: Laboratory automation and simulation is the part of AI research that connects software to physical experiments. AI systems read instrument streams, propose changes to protocols, run simulations of experiments, and schedule robotic equipment. In self-driving labs, models choose next experiments and execute them through liquid handlers and analytical instruments. Digital twins create a computational replica of a lab setup or a biological system so that many conditions can be tested before any physical run. AI also forecasts consumable demand and optimises protocols by searching parameter spaces. These are working systems in some labs, not just concepts, though most operate in narrow domains.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some pieces are mature, such as instrument data pipelines that stream and clean sensor readings at scale and optimisation algorithms that tune known protocols. Digital twins are useful when the underlying physics or biology is well characterised. Self-driving labs have demonstrated closed-loop cycles in specific tasks, such as reaction optimisation or material discovery. What is not solved is general autonomy across messy, changing lab environments, and many systems still need human intervention for sample preparation, error recovery, and safety checks. Data quality, reproducibility, and integration between instruments remain hard limits. Simulation fidelity also drops when the system is complex or poorly measured.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The page on Self-Driving Laboratories gives the broadest view of closed-loop experiment planning and robotic execution. Digital Twins for Experiments explains how simulation models are built and where they diverge from reality. Instrument and Sensor Data covers the raw signals and calibration work that feed every other page. Optimising Lab Protocols focuses on search methods for experimental parameters and sequences, while Forecasting Lab Supplies looks at demand prediction and inventory planning for reagents and consumables. A reader can start with instrument data for foundations, move to digital twins and protocol optimisation for methods, then use self-driving labs and supply forecasting to see full workflows. The site's library of 135 research papers and 11795 extracted claims can support that path, with links to original papers rather than a search tool.
